# CEGR: CounterExample-Guided Reward Design with Multi-Tier GateKeeper Verification

[![Python 3.9+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.9+-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

**CEGR (CounterExample-Guided Reward Design)** is a principled framework for synthesizing and repairing reinforcement learning reward functions generated by Large Language Models (LLMs). By combining static anti-hack AST verification, dynamic counterexample generation (via DP and continuous trajectory attackers), trajectory preference evaluation (TPE), signal correlation filtering, and short RL probes, CEGR eliminates reward hacking with strict budget fairness ($N = 4$).

---

## 1. Key Features

- **Multi-Domain Adaptability:** Seamless support across tabular discrete domains (**Minigrid DoorKey-5x5, 6x6, 8x8**) and continuous control robotic manipulation (**Meta-World** tasks like `reach-v2`, `door-open-v2`, `pick-place-v2`).
- **5-Tier GateKeeper Verification (G1–G5):**
  - **G1 (Sandbox Execution):** Safe Python compilation and runtime validation with `math` and vectorized `numpy` support.
  - **G2 (Static Anti-Hack):** AST inspection catching missing goals, unconditional survival bonuses, no-op farming, and positive L2 distance exploits.
  - **G3 (TPE & Attacker):** Trajectory preference evaluation against reference pairs $P_0$ and accumulated counterexamples, paired with DP/Continuous Trajectory Attackers.
  - **G4 (Signal & Correlation):** Milestone separation checks, stage variance validation, and rank correlation ($\rho \ge 0.75$).
  - **G5 (RL Probe):** Fast tabular Q-learning or continuous SAC/PPO probe detecting unlearnable reward functions.
- **Fair Baseline Comparisons:** Identical LLM base model (`Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-AWQ`), identical call budget ($N = 4$), identical interface signature (`reward_components(s, a, s2) -> dict`), and strictly independent Oracle evaluation.
  - Baselines: **ORIG**, **EUREKA** (evolutionary search with training reflection), **CARD** (static TPE), and **CARD_REFL** (TPE with text memory).
  - 6 Ablation Variants: `noPool`, `noAnchors`, `noClass`, `noG2`, `noG4`, `noG5`.

## 2. Directory Layout

```text
CEGR/
├── data/                                   # Frozen datasets (100% reproducible)
│   ├── doorkey/                            # Tabular DoorKey manifests & reference trajs
│   └── metaworld/                          # Continuous Meta-World manifests & trajs
├── configs/                                # Hyperparameter & ablation YAML configs
│   ├── doorkey_config.yaml
│   ├── metaworld_config.yaml
│   └── ablations.yaml
├── cegr/                                   # Main Python package
│   ├── envs/                               # Environment wrappers (DoorKey & Meta-World)
│   ├── core/                               # Code sandbox, TPE evaluator, base runner
│   ├── solvers/                            # DP solver, trajectory attacker, RL probes, Oracle VF
│   ├── engine/                             # Unified vLLM inference engine
│   ├── baselines/                          # ORIG, Eureka, CARD & CARD_REFL implementations
│   ├── synthesis/                          # CEGR 5-tier GateKeeper, CE pool, assimilator, anchors
│   └── eval/                               # Paired cluster bootstrap & LaTeX/plot generators
├── notebooks/                              # Kaggle GPU execution notebooks
│   ├── cegr_runner.ipynb
│   ├── metaworld_benchmark.ipynb
│   ├── baseline_eureka.ipynb
│   └── baseline_card.ipynb
├── tests/                                  # Unit tests runnable offline
├── requirements.txt
├── setup.py
└── README.md
```

---

## 3. Installation & Quick Start

### Local / Kaggle Setup
```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/CEGR.git
cd CEGR
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install -e .
```

### Running Offline Unit Tests
Verify all gates, solvers, and baselines logic without requiring GPU or LLM inference:
```bash
pytest tests/
```

### Running on Kaggle GPU
Open `notebooks/cegr_runner.ipynb` in Kaggle (2x T4 or A100 GPU), configure your experiment mode in the configuration cell, and run end-to-end.
